subject: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close

Team —

Quick context: ACME (large finance customer) is ready to sign but procurement has two technical asks in parallel with legal: an auditable export of request/response logs (90-day window) with redaction controls, and an on-demand bulk export that matches their internal schema for ingestion. They also want an API-level flag to pin to a particular inference model (same major model but specific variant) for compliance.

Why this matters: closing this deal moves us into a preferred vendor slot and unlocks marketplace listing for the finance vertical. They need an implementation plan and rough ETA for pricing negotiation by EOD Friday (their procurement deadline).

Asks:
- Can Eng give feasibility notes + rough implementation approach for: 1) export endpoint (S3-compatible manifest + CSV/JSON) and 2) route-level model pin flag?
- Security/compliance: can CS/Neha confirm acceptable redaction scope and whether sample export (masked) is sufficient for SOC evidence?
- Dev: best-case timeline for a minimum viable delivery (inc. tests + docs) and any blocking infra changes?

Attachments: I attached current SOW draft and their compliance matrix.

Next steps: I need a short playbook (one paragraph + ETA) to share with Acme procurement by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-Acme-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 142KB)
Attachment: acme-compliance-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 68KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close

Thanks Marcus — looping in a couple quick questions to scope compliance:

- Redaction: do they require PII-stripping algorithm or are token-level hashes acceptable (they mentioned "redacted but linkable to audit id")?
- Retention window: 90 days is fine; will they accept a streaming export (incremental daily manifests) or do they need ad-hoc one-off full dumps?

From a CS perspective, a sample masked export is usually enough for initial sign-off if we include an attestation and retention policy. If Legal wants raw plaintext logs under NDA, we'll need a change to our data access controls (we should factor that into timeline).

Marcus — can you confirm if Acme's legal has asked for raw logs under NDA? If not, we should push for masked samples + attestations to avoid changing infra access patterns.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close

Quick feasibility note from Eng:

- Export endpoint: doable as a feature on top of our existing audit pipeline. Minimal MVP: a scheduled job that writes daily gzipped JSON exports to an S3 bucket (customer-managed or our bucket with customer-specific prefix) + a manifest JSON describing files and last-event timestamp. Add a small API to request an on-demand export (trigger and return manifest link). Estimated dev effort: 2-3 sprints (4-6 weeks) to ship with tests and docs if prioritized.

- Redaction: we can provide token-level hashing + configurable redaction rules (PII patterns). Delivering a provably "raw logs under NDA" path is more invasive (requires privileged access paths + audit controls). Adding that would be another 2-3 weeks and requires security review.

- Route-level model pin: low complexity — add route config to persist a pinned model variant and fallback behavior. Should be a 1-sprint (2 weeks) delivery including console UI and API.

Blockers / notes:
- We need Product sign-off on retention/default redaction policy and whether we want to offer "raw-logs under NDA" as an escape hatch (affects infra & audit).
- Dev time estimates assume no major schema refactor for the audit pipeline.

If Product approves a narrow MVP (daily export + on-demand manifest + pin flag) we can target a 4-week timeline. If Acme insists on raw logs, timeline moves to ~6-8 weeks.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Paul Sanders <paul.sanders@acmefinance.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@acmefinance.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close

Marcus / Neha — appreciate the diligence. A few clarifications from Acme procurement:

- Masked exports are acceptable for initial security review, but legal will require the ability for "forensic export" under strict controls if we encounter incidents. For signing, we need: 1) a masked sample export this week and 2) a written commitment/plan that forensic export under NDA is possible within "x" weeks.
- Model pinning: must be available via API; console is nice-to-have.
- Their SRE wants the export to be S3-compatible and use a naming convention to slot into their ingestion pipeline.

Their sign-off deadline for procurement is next Thursday (18 Nov). I know that's tight — is the sample masked export possible before EOD Friday (13 Nov)? If yes, we'll keep the schedule.

Paul Sanders
Director, IT Procurement — Acme Finance
paul.sanders@acmefinance.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: export & audit hooks — escalation for close

Follow-up playbook (short) to share with Acme procurement — ready to send from Sales:

1) Masked sample export (what we'll deliver this week):
- Deliverable: single-day masked export (gzipped JSON) matching their schema columns + manifest file. Redaction: token-level hashing for PII fields; sample will include attestations about redaction rules.
- ETA: deliver sample by EOD Friday 13 Nov. (Dev will run an on-demand export from staging and sanitize per CS guidance.)

2) Model pinning (MVP):
- Deliverable: API flag to pin route to a specific model variant, with fallback policy. Console UI to follow.
- ETA: 2 weeks for API + backend (target 27 Nov), 1 additional sprint for console UX if prioritized.

3) Forensic/raw export under NDA (escape hatch):
- Deliverable: documented process + timeline to enable forensic export under NDA. This requires Security review and privileged access controls.
- ETA: 4-6 weeks from sign-off (security review dependent).

Risks & notes: if Acme requires immediate raw-log access prior to signing, we need an approval from Security and Product to open privileged paths — this will slip schedule. Otherwise the masked-sample path is a low-friction compromise.

Action items for Marcus (Sales):
- Send the sample delivery commitment to Acme procurement (I drafted the line below).
- Confirm whether Acme prefers our S3 or their S3 (Dev: please confirm cross-account copy is supported in staging).

Draft sentence for Marcus to send to Acme: "We will deliver a masked sample export that matches the attached schema by EOD Friday 13 Nov and provide a documented plan to enable forensic export under NDA within 4–6 weeks of sign-off."

I'll pick up Security sign-off cadence and start the intake for the privileged access path if Acme opts for the forensic export.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com
